description: Sixteen voices that drift as a cloud around one pitch and can be drawn onto a chord by a control voltage

inputs.text: Sets the centre pitch of the cloud at 1V per octave, with the voices spread six semitones either side of it
A polyphonic cable whose channels are the pitches the voices converge on, at 1V per octave
0V locks the sixteen voices onto the chord at the chord input; 9V or more scatters them into the drifting cloud; between the two the voices cross over on an S-curve

outputs.text: Sixteen channels of pitch, at 1V per octave

notes: the converge input reads 0V when nothing is patched, which is full lock, so the cloud never appears until that input is raised.
the output always carries sixteen channels, however many the chord input carries; the chord's channels are repeated to fill them, and with nothing patched there every voice converges on 0V.
the centre pitch is shifted by whole octaves whenever it would carry the cloud outside -4V to 5V, so a swept root jumps an octave rather than running off either end.
each voice wanders a tenth of an octave either side of its place in the cloud, moving at a fifth of a volt per second toward a fresh random target.

inputs.0: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
inputs.2:
0 to 10V · continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
